thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: sustained CUDA OOMs observed from hotrod-decode pool (decode/stream path). Error spike started ~1729471000, currently 5xx + OOM traces. Runbook: decode-gpu-oom. @sara_oncall you are paged.

sara_oncall: On it. pulling logs from node group. Any obvious config changes that could cause runaway generation?

matt_runtime: Not seeing config pushes in last hour. Telemetry shows sudden increase in long streaming sessions with max_tokens unset for some clients. Might be header parsing bug causing token cap to be ignored.

julia_sre: Node list: hotrod-decode-{03,04,07} are showing repeated CUDA OOMs and container restarts. kube restarts: 03 x5, 04 x8, 07 x3 in last 6m. Eviction loops present.

leo_support: Customer impact: alerts from support — 3 customers reporting partial failures: acme-inc (50% streams dropped), blue-ride (30%), zephyr-labs (40%). Opening tickets T-789, T-790, T-791.

matt_runtime: Dumping one sample stack: ```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.2 GiB (GPU 0; 16.00 GiB total, 12.4 GiB already allocated)
  File \"/srv/runtime/decode_stream.py\", line 412, in _decode_step
    out = kernel_runner.step(*args)
  File \"/srv/runtime/kernel_runner.cpp\", line 88, in run
    cudaLaunchKernel(...)
```

sara_oncall: Quick mitigations I'm going to apply now:
  1) throttle streaming concurrency for hotrod-decode to 30% (temp) via rate-limit rule
  2) enforce max_output_tokens header default to 512 for streaming route
  3) add fallback route to small-quant model variant (cpu-safe) for requests over 512 tokens
  4) cordon node hotrod-decode-04 if restarts continue

julia_sre: +1. Please add a temporary traffic-shed so we don't thrash the autoscaler. I'll watch kube restarts and ensure OOMs stop.

sara_oncall: Applying rate-limit change: ```
redwoodctl routes update --route decode-stream --rate-limit "concurrency=200" --env hotrod
```

matt_runtime: Patching header enforcement on gateway to default max_output_tokens: ```
kubectl patch configmap gateway-rules -n redwood --type merge -p '{"data":{"default_max_output_tokens":"512"}}'
```

telemetry-bot: Telemetry update: error_rate for decode/stream jumped to 8.4% (baseline 0.3%). Avg tokens/request in spike cohort = 3.4k. KV cache growth correlated with long tails.

leo_support: Notifying affected customers with a short status note. Draft: "We're investigating increased failures on streaming. We're applying throttles and fallbacks; engineers are on it. ETA 30m." Want to send? :point_up:

nina_product: Send it and include temporary mitigation steps and workaround: set client max_output_tokens or use polling generation to keep requests smaller.

sara_oncall: Throttle applied. Observing connection drain — OOMs dropped from 6/min -> 1/min over the last 90s. Node hotrod-decode-04 still restarting (2x). Cordon it now.

julia_sre: cordon/evict done for hotrod-decode-04: ```
kubectl cordon hotrod-decode-04 && kubectl drain hotrod-decode-04 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

matt_runtime: While node is drained, I'm enabling fallback model routing for requests that exceed the new header cap. Patch applied to routing policy, fallback hit-rate started ~40% for the spike cohort.

telemetry-bot: After mitigations: error_rate down to 2.1%. Request drop incidents per min decreased 80%. Customer impact severity reduced but some ticket failures persist (intermittent).

leo_support: Sent status update to customers T-789/T-790/T-791. Included actionable workaround and note about follow-up when we have full remediation.

sara_oncall: Handing off to @matt_runtime and @julia_sre for deeper root cause & remediation. I'm stepping out for a quick break — will monitor slack ping.

matt_runtime: A few follow-ups for post-incident actions:
  - roll out header validation unit to reject requests missing max_output_tokens (short-term)
  - add regression test for streaming header parsing
  - investigate model quantization path that may be allocating unexpectedly large temporary tensors during decode
  - add KV cache cap per-session and early-eviction for long-tail requests

julia_sre: Infra follow-ups:
  - add an autoscaler cooldown when OOM restart loop triggered to avoid thrash
  - add node-level OOM alerts with actionable suggested remediations in playbook
  - ensure cordoned nodes don't autojoin until manual triage

matt_runtime: Root cause hypothesis: malformed client header plus unset token cap allowed runaway generation that grew KV cache + temp kernel allocations triggering CUDA OOM on 16GB instances. Need reproducer.

nina_product: Please prioritize customer-facing postmortem: summary, timeline, customer impact (requests dropped, ticket ids), and remediation timeline. Product will own the customer comms for the next 24h.

julia_sre: Currently all hotrod-decode nodes stable, OOMs ceased after throttles and cordon. Marking incident state: mitigated. Will keep the thread open for RCA and follow-ups.

incident-bot: Incident state -> mitigated. Pager cleared for oncall rotations. :white_check_mark:

matt_runtime: Capturing logs and a minimal repro. Will post a link to the repro and changeset in the RCA doc. Assigning follow-ups in the incident tracker.

sara_oncall: Back from break, ack handoff. Thanks team for quick action.

leo_support: Closing customer communications loop: customers acknowledged the note and asked to be notified when RCA is ready.

telemetry-bot: Final snapshot at 1729471449: error_rate 0.9%, fallback hit 28% for offending cohort, avg tokens/request returned to baseline 290.

matt_runtime: Next steps tracked in IRIS-4321. I'll kick off a postmortem draft tomorrow AM.

julia_sre: Leaving the thread open for 24h for any regressions. If no further OOMs, we'll archive and publish the postmortem.

incident-bot: END_OF_THREAD"
